prior_summary: Attachment as an action-conditioned invariant: an original joint/gripper action diffusion model is conditioned on learned exclusive none/red/blue attachment beliefs and structured TCP/object forecasts. Attached forecasts compose a learned slowly varying TCP-to-object transform; independent forecasts have separate support-motion branches. Future pose, regime, rigidity, stationary-object and low-noise denoising-consequence losses train this distinction over the complete expanded slice.
applicable_conditions: World-frame tracked TCP and both cube poses with wxyz quaternions, measured Panda qpos/qvel and both goals. Nominal parallel-jaw pickups and the incoming red lowering/release/empty retreat before blue pickup are supported. Causal two-observation history must distinguish attached payload identity from the next block. No explicit requested-object, past-command, image or force channel is present in this model.
termination_guidance: Prefer transfer once the intended object is elevated and co-moving with TCP with approximately constant relative pose and demonstrated closed finger width, while the previously placed object stays settled. Endpoints already translate goalward; neither one exact pose nor zero velocity is required. During ambiguous closure or incomplete incoming release, continue locally or transfer with explicit uncertainty to a successor supporting the overlap. These cues do not add conditions to task success.
limitations: Nominal successful demonstrations cannot calibrate miss/slip probabilities or safe rejection thresholds. The fixed single-sample DDPM interface has no candidate-ranking hook, so forecast-conditioned denoising and a confidence-weighted training consequence loss replace, but are not equivalent to, multi-sample ranking. Residual-scale prediction is not calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Requested identity is inferred from ordered geometry and demonstrated context, not a supplied role. No IK, force model, guaranteed collision avoidance, action equivariance, replay or scripted controller is implemented.

config.segmentation: All 24 assigned expanded acquire_block slices, unchanged; all valid action and future slots are used, including incoming placement, release, retreat and outgoing lifted translation.
config.normalization: Use supplied complete-demonstration observation half ranges and original-action affine normalization. No per-skill refit. World relative positions use shared TCP xyz half ranges; TCP-frame relative positions use their maximum.
config.action_representation: Eight common encoded native absolute joint/gripper actions; external fixed sampler performs decoding and bounds handling.
config.selection: Last EMA at the fixed 20000-update budget, without performance-based selection.

architecture.forecast_uncertainty: Learned bounded normalized position residual scale for TCP, red and blue. Not a safety or failure certificate.

label_parameters.comment: Training-only kinematic proxy thresholds in physical units, not deployment acceptance gates or new normalizers.

adaptations: No inference candidate selection or likelihood fallback is available; use noisy-action-conditioned forecasts in every epsilon call and distill clean-estimate consequences through frozen forecast weights during training.
Only two observations are supplied. Observed pose differences and qvel replace a longer attachment history; past actions and explicit requested role are not synthesized.
Both color identities are retained. A three-class belief enforces exclusive attachment but does not hard-code red-first actions.
Future poses and expert commands supervise the forecast and regime labels only. Deployment receives only noisy candidate actions, diffusion timestep and causal raw observations.
